skill.name: appinsights-instrumentation
skill.description: Guides teams through Azure Application Insights instrumentation for ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Python, and Azure Container Apps using Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry references, resource setup guidance, and configuration examples.
skill.summary: Instrument web apps with Azure Application Insights and Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from documentation links, Azure Portal templates, SDK configuration examples, and monitoring queries. One medium-confidence issue remains where the Container Apps guide retrieves a Log Analytics shared key in a shell variable, and one low-severity semantic issue exposes an Application Insights connection string as a Bicep output. No prompt injection, malicious command intent, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Log Analytics workspace shared key is handled in a shell workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed Azure Monitor destination or secret-backed automation where possible. Warn users not to print, commit, or store workspace shared keys in shell history.

remediation.issue: Application Insights connection string is exposed as a Bicep deployment output.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the connection string output unless it is required. Store the value directly in Azure app settings, Container Apps secrets, or controlled deployment secrets.

finding_verdicts.reason: The Bicep line assigns the Application Insights resource to a Log Analytics workspace created in the same template. It does not enumerate the host system or collect reconnaissance data.
The detected sequence is a Markdown link to ../scripts/appinsights.ps1 for reference documentation. It does not read files, write files, or accept user-controlled paths.
The relative path is another Markdown reference to the local script example. It is documentation navigation, not filesystem traversal or local file access.
The URL is an Azure Portal template with placeholders for a user-selected App Service resource. It is not an automatic outbound request or hidden endpoint.
The command substitution queries a Log Analytics workspace customer ID with Azure CLI placeholder arguments. It does not execute untrusted input or create a command injection path.

The snippet retrieves a Log Analytics workspace primary shared key into a shell variable for environment creation. This is legitimate Azure setup guidance, but shared keys are sensitive and can leak through shell history, logs, or later command arguments.
The line names common HTTP client libraries as examples of instrumented dependencies. It does not perform a network request or define an external destination.
The KQL example expands Container Apps environment variable metadata to check for an Application Insights setting by name. It does not read local environment files or output secret values.
The flag passes a known workspace ID into an Azure Container Apps environment creation example. It does not collect system information from the user environment.
The text only advises calling the telemetry setup after dotenv loads configuration. It does not access or disclose environment variables itself.
The snippet reads APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING to configure the Azure Monitor SDK. This is standard configuration access and is not paired with logging, file writes, or exfiltration.

The environment object is used only to pass the Application Insights connection string into the SDK. There is no enumeration of all environment variables or network disclosure beyond intended telemetry configuration.
The line reads a named environment variable in a TypeScript quick start. It does not access environment files, print the value, or send it to an unrelated service.

content.value_statement: Teams often need consistent telemetry across Azure web apps and services. This skill provides focused Application Insights guidance, SDK setup paths, and Azure Container Apps observability references.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Azure App Service auto-instrumentation for ASP.NET Core and Node.js apps.
Shows package and startup changes for ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python instrumentation.
Provides Bicep and Azure CLI references for creating Application Insights resources.
Guides connection string configuration with environment variables and Container Apps secrets.
Summarizes Container Apps logs, metrics, distributed tracing, Dapr tracing, and KQL queries.
Links to Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry quick references for Python, TypeScript, and Java exporters.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not safely automate project changes by itself.
It assumes the application runs on Azure or can send telemetry to Azure Monitor.
It does not replace current Microsoft Learn documentation for pricing, quotas, or service limits.
Some SDK quick references are condensed and defer advanced patterns to other skills.

use_cases.title: Plan App Service Instrumentation
use_cases.description: Choose auto-instrumentation or SDK setup for an ASP.NET Core or Node.js app hosted in Azure App Service.

use_cases.title: Standardize Container Apps Observability
use_cases.description: Configure Log Analytics, Application Insights connection strings, and tracing patterns for Azure Container Apps environments.

use_cases.title: Review Telemetry Coverage
use_cases.description: Use KQL examples and monitoring checks to find services without Application Insights telemetry.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Instrumentation Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure web app context and tell me whether auto-instrumentation or SDK instrumentation is the better path. Ask for missing hosting details.

prompt_templates.title: Add SDK Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Application Insights SDK setup steps for my ASP.NET Core, Node.js, or Python app. List the files I should inspect before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Design Container Apps Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an observability plan for an Azure Container Apps environment with shared Log Analytics, Application Insights, distributed tracing, and validation queries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Telemetry Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this service inventory and identify missing Application Insights configuration, connection string handling risks, and KQL checks for follow-up.

output_examples.input: I have a Node.js App Service and want request tracing in Application Insights.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use Azure App Service auto-instrumentation first if supported. Otherwise, install Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry, initialize it before app startup, and set the connection string as an app setting.

output_examples.input: Our Container Apps environment has logs but no request latency.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that built-in metrics cover infrastructure only. It recommends adding Application Insights SDKs, setting a shared connection string, and validating traces in Application Map.

output_examples.input: I need to know which services lack App Insights.
output_examples.output: It suggests Azure Resource Graph and KQL checks that inspect container app environment variables and summarize services missing the Application Insights connection string.

best_practices: Confirm the language, framework, and Azure hosting model before selecting instrumentation guidance.
Store connection strings in platform configuration or secrets, not in source files.
Validate telemetry with Application Map, Log Analytics tables, and request-level queries after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not add instrumentation before confirming where the application is hosted.
Do not place Application Insights connection strings in appsettings.json or source control.
Do not assume Container Apps infrastructure metrics include request tracing.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and references. Use a separate automation workflow to apply changes.

faq.question: Which apps are covered?
faq.answer: It covers ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Python, and Azure Container Apps guidance, with some SDK references for TypeScript and Java.

faq.question: Can it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: It includes Bicep and Azure CLI examples, but you choose and run any resource changes.

faq.question: How should connection strings be handled?
faq.answer: Use Azure app settings, Container Apps secrets, or infrastructure templates. Do not store them in source files.

faq.question: Does it support auto-instrumentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Azure Portal auto-instrumentation for supported Azure App Service ASP.NET Core and Node.js apps.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for Microsoft Learn?
faq.answer: No. Use Microsoft Learn for the latest service limits, pricing, and official support details.
